question: What can make HbA1c, the standard long-term blood sugar test, read falsely reassuring?
answer: Red blood cells that die young. HbA1c measures how much haemoglobin has picked up sugar; a red cell lives about 120 days, so it averages two to three months. When cells are lost early, through haemolysis, bleeding or transfusion, they have less time to collect sugar. The number drops while the glucose does not.
move: Know how long a measure takes to fill before reading its level.
ask: Which measure I rely on is really an average over a long stretch, hiding what happened recently?
source: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care, 2024
